lyndal-stephens-greth.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
lyndal-stephens-greth.period: Endeavor Energy Resources sale to Diamondback, announced February 2024 and completed September 2024
lyndal-stephens-greth.summary: Narrow review found no documented political-leverage, preferential-benefit or exchange evidence concerning Lyndal Stephens Greth or her family. The only readable material concerns the family oil company and its sale. This is not exoneration; coverage was thin and several sources were unreadable.

support.text: A tertiary reference describes Autry Stephens as founder of Endeavor Energy Resources and reports its 2024 sale to Diamondback Energy for about $26 billion. It does not name Lyndal Stephens Greth. It is context for the source of the family fortune, not evidence of a political mechanism.
support.access: Page text reviewed; heirs not named

counter.text: The same article contains no information on political donations or government relationships. This limits the review; it does not show an absence of such activity.

The Forbes Czech list page for this entry was reachable only as a title, so its figures and family composition could not be checked. A search-result summary attributed to Bloomberg a Diamondback stake of about 30%; Bloomberg returned HTTP 403 and that figure is unverified here.
counter.source: Forbes CZ: Lyndal Stephens Greth s rodinou
counter.access: Only the page title was readable

lyndal-stephens-greth.limitations: Family entry: evidence about Autry Stephens, the late founder, must not be attributed to Lyndal Stephens Greth or other relatives. Searches covered donations and political ties only through general queries; FEC and lobbying records were not checked. Oil and gas regulation, federal leasing and Texas policy were not examined. Wealth, inheritance and industry alone justify no points. This is a narrow review, not an exoneration.

francois-pinault.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
francois-pinault.summary: The only reviewed material is the 2019 pledge of €100 million to Notre-Dame by the Pinault family through Artemis. A charitable pledge is not a preferential benefit. Older leads about state-linked financing and political networks in France could not be read, so this entry establishes nothing either way.

support.text: The Pinault family, through Artemis, pledged €100 million to rebuild Notre-Dame; Francois-Henri Pinault, chairman and CEO of Kering, and his father François Pinault issued the statement. This documents a public gift and no return benefit.
support.access: Page text reviewed; the page date and weekday reference are inconsistent

counter.text: The article does not mention tax deductions or any government favor. The reviewed evidence provides no link between the gift and any benefit.

The Le Monde diplomatique 2003 article on public money and private fortunes and a 1995 Le Monde piece on political networks in large companies were discovery leads; both fetches failed and nothing from them is used.

francois-pinault.limitations: Family entry: François Pinault and François-Henri Pinault are distinct people and evidence about one cannot be transferred to the other. Luxury-sector regulation, Kering, Artemis holdings, media ownership and 1990s French financing history were not examined. Not exoneration.

mackenzie-scott.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
mackenzie-scott.summary: No evidence of political leverage, preferential benefit or an exchange was found. Her documented activity is large-scale philanthropy. Her wealth derives from Amazon shares, and Jeff Bezos’s conduct is not hers. This reflects a narrow review; absence of evidence here does not prove an absence of political activity.

support.text: A tertiary reference reports that Scott signed the Giving Pledge in May 2019, gave $14 billion in 2022, announced $640 million in March 2024, and reached about $26.3 billion given by end of 2025. A 2020 post listed democracy among focus areas. This is context, not evidence of any political-power mechanism.

counter.text: The article describes no donations to candidates or parties and no government relationships. This is a limit of coverage, not a certification.
An AP article on her 2025 giving (a discovery lead) could not be fetched, so none of its content is used here.
counter.source: AP: MacKenzie Scott gave $7.1 billion in 2025

mackenzie-scott.limitations: FEC and lobbying records were not checked; political giving through PACs or ballot measures was not searched individually. Philanthropy influences civil society but is not scored as a wealth–power mechanism without specific evidence. Not exoneration.

emmanuel-besnier.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
emmanuel-besnier.period: Aid year 2023; tax settlement December 2024; Senate hearing June 17, 2025
emmanuel-besnier.summary: Besnier’s June 2025 Senate testimony documents state aid to Lactalis and a €475 million tax settlement, which he and his finance director characterized differently from the rapporteur. The reviewed record shows a contested fiscal settlement and ordinary aid schemes, not a preferential political exchange.
emmanuel-besnier.mechanism: Public aid and tax settlement; political leverage and exchange not established

support.text: At the Senate inquiry, Lactalis reported €18.7 million of public aid in 2023 (€1.8 million equipment, €12.3 million social schemes, €4.6 million tax credits). Besnier confirmed a €475 million settlement with the tax authority covering 2006–2019, which the rapporteur tied to subsidiary arrangements.
support.source: Sénat: commission d’enquête sur les aides publiques aux entreprises, compte rendu
support.access: Page text reviewed via fetch summary

support.text: Public Sénat reports the rapporteur’s account of the arrangements through Belgian and Luxembourg subsidiaries and states that a criminal investigation for aggravated tax fraud is ongoing.
support.kind: Press report of allegation and open investigation

counter.text: Besnier called the rapporteur’s description “totalement inexact”, and the finance director called it an “imaginary scheme”; Besnier said he preferred to settle the past despite an interpretation dispute. He argued aid only partly offsets high labor charges and said social aid was 1.3% of total labor cost.
counter.access: Page text reviewed via fetch summary

counter.text: Aid of €18.7 million and a negotiated settlement with a tax authority are not themselves evidence of political influence; the reviewed records show no link between either and a political relationship.
counter.access: Page text reviewed via fetch summary

emmanuel-besnier.limitations: The criminal investigation is an open matter, with no charge or finding in the sources read; no guilt is implied. Le Monde pieces on his tax negotiations and the 2017 infant-milk contamination case were not readable and not assessed. Political contacts and agricultural policy influence were not examined. Not exoneration.

lei-jun.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
lei-jun.period: Xiaomi Phase II factory approval, June 2021; NPC deputy roles from 2013
lei-jun.summary: Beijing’s planning authority describes an expedited Xiaomi factory approval in June 2021 as an institutional “Xiaomi model”, and Lei Jun is a long-serving National People’s Congress deputy. Neither fact, on its own, establishes personal patronage or an exchange; the same page says the land was obtained through a public listing.
lei-jun.mechanism: Local government approval process for a corporate project; personal exchange not established

support.text: A Beijing planning-authority account dated June 30, 2021 says Xiaomi obtained two plots on June 29 and the Changping branch approved the design plan on June 30 through a “multi-plan integration” review; the project is planned for 10 million phones a year, worth about 60 billion yuan, and the process was called the “Xiaomi model”.
support.source: Beijing Municipal Planning and Natural Resources Commission
support.access: Page text reviewed (Chinese, summarized by fetch tool)

support.text: A tertiary reference lists Lei Jun as a deputy of the Beijing Municipal People’s Congress (2012) and of the National People’s Congress from 2013, including the 14th NPC from 2023, and a 2019 official recognition as an Outstanding Builder of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics.

counter.text: The planning page says the land was obtained through a public listing and describes the process as institutional reform and a model for attracting “high-end, cutting-edge” enterprises generally. This points to a policy template for the district, not necessarily a favor for one founder.
counter.source: Beijing Municipal Planning and Natural Resources Commission
counter.kind: Alternative explanation within the primary source
counter.access: Page text reviewed (Chinese, summarized by fetch tool)

counter.text: The Wikipedia article reports no proposals made by Lei Jun as a deputy. Office-holding alone justifies no points. The Xiaomi 2021 interim report listed in the project handoff was a binary PDF whose text could not be read here.
counter.source: Wikipedia: Lei Jun; Xiaomi interim report
counter.access: PDF not readable as text in this session

lei-jun.limitations: The factory approval is distinct from electric-vehicle projects, later legislative proposals and subsidies, none of which were reviewed. The legislative-body membership in China is not equivalent to independent political leverage. The 2021 Pentagon list episode is a US government matter, not examined. Not exoneration.

andreas-von-bechtolsheim.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
andreas-von-bechtolsheim.summary: No evidence of political leverage, preferential benefit or an exchange was found. The reviewed reference describes a technology-founder fortune from Sun, Cisco, Google and Arista. A 2024 SEC settlement is a securities matter, not a wealth–power mechanism. This is a narrow review, not exoneration.

support.text: A tertiary reference reports he co-founded Sun Microsystems, sold Granite Systems to Cisco in 1996, co-founded Arista Networks and invested $100,000 in Google in 1998 alongside David Cheriton. It says DARPA supported the early SUN project. This is context for wealth, not evidence of a mechanism.

counter.text: The article reports no political donations, government roles or lobbying. This limits the review rather than certifying absence.

The article says he settled 2024 SEC insider-trading allegations about information on Cisco’s proposed Acacia acquisition, paying a civil penalty of nearly $1 million and accepting a five-year officer-and-director bar. This is a market-conduct matter and is not scored as political leverage or benefit.
counter.access: Page text reviewed; SEC order itself not opened

andreas-von-bechtolsheim.limitations: Family entry: evidence concerns Andreas von Bechtolsheim himself; other family members were not researched. FEC and lobbying records, Arista’s government sales and German policy contacts were not checked. A German 2014 Tagesspiegel article from the discovery leads does not mention him. Not exoneration.

cyrus-poonawalla.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed
cyrus-poonawalla.summary: The reviewed feature documents that the Indian government bought Serum Institute’s COVID vaccine at a low price and advanced Rs 3,000 crore in April 2021, while also describing a strained relationship. These are company-level transactions in a public-health emergency, in which Adar Poonawalla was the public face; they do not show an exchange involving Cyrus Poonawalla personally.
cyrus-poonawalla.mechanism: Government vaccine procurement and advance; personal exchange not established

support.text: Open magazine reports the government bought doses at about US$2 each and advanced Rs 3,000 crore to Serum Institute in April 2021, after Covishield exports were banned.
support.source: Open Magazine: The Legend of the Poonawallas
support.access: Page text reviewed via fetch summary; article date not confirmed

counter.text: The same feature says the dose price was roughly one-tenth of the global average, that the relationship became strained, that chief ministers made threatening calls to Adar Poonawalla, and that the family were scapegoats for delayed government orders. It reports few political ties for Cyrus Poonawalla beyond a photo with Pranab Mukherjee.
counter.access: Page text reviewed via fetch summary

counter.text: Discovery leads on Panama Papers property attachments of Poonawalla relatives (Times of India) and fact-checks on Serum’s political donation channel could not be read, so nothing from them is used. No relative’s case is attributed to Cyrus Poonawalla.

cyrus-poonawalla.limitations: Identity: Cyrus Poonawalla founded Serum Institute and his son Adar runs it; most reporting concerns Adar or the company. Serum’s political donations, price terms and advance conditions were not verified from primary records. Public-health procurement may have legitimate purposes. Not exoneration.
